**Looking the role up once:** the first call to `get()` finds the role and stores it on the object, and later calls reuse it. A separate flag records that the lookup has already happened, so a missing role isn't looked up again either. I didn't use the existing `Role::getSystemRole()` for two reasons:
- Its `isset` check fails when the result is `null`, so a missing admin role would be looked up on every call.

**Registration:** I added `$this->app->scoped(AdminRecipients::class)` in `AppServiceProvider::register()`. A "scoped" binding means the container shares one instance within a request or queued job and starts a fresh one for the next. So you need to get the class from the container (constructor injection or `app(AdminRecipients::class)`). Creating it with `new` gives you a separate instance that does its own lookup.

The list of users itself isn't cached. Each call to `get()` still fetches them, so changes to who holds the role show up straight away.
